شراء مستمرة هنا لأننا استهلكنا بالفعل معظم نطاقنا اليومي. الآن، في مثال الاستمرار هذا، هنا يمكنك رؤية استمرارات بعد الوصول إلى أعلى مستوى لليوم السابق، لماذا؟ لأننا استخدمنا جزءاً صغيراً فقط من متوسط نطاقنا اليومي، لذا يمكننا توقع استمرار وتوسع، خاصة نحو هدفنا السابق. دعونا ننتقل إلى مثال آخر. هنا في مثالنا التالي، يبلغ متوسط نطاقنا اليومي حوالي 400 نقطة. بالنظر إلى مكان تشكل السعر، إذا ارتفعنا 400 نقطة، ما الذي يمكننا الوصول إليه؟ كما تعلم، يمكننا الوصول إلى كل تقلبات الفشل هذه هنا. لذا، ستكون تلك هدفاً جيداً للبحث عنه. الآن ، دعونا نرى ما سيحدث، أليس كذلك؟ نحن نرى حركة معاكسة كبيرة. لذا، يجب أن نفكر في كيفية تأثير ذلك على نطاقنا اليومي. إذا ألقيت نظرة، فلو كان لدينا ذيل صغير يحترم مستوى التوازن (EQ)، لتمكنا من الوصول إلى هذه القمم بحوالي 300 نقطة. هذا كافٍ تماماً مع متوسط نطاقنا اليومي الحالي. ولكن عندما نواجه حركة معاكسة كبيرة، فإن هذا يستهلك الوقت والنطاق. لذا الآن يجب أن نحصل على ماذا؟ يجب أن يكون لدينا نطاق يتجاوز ذلك المتوسط للوصول إلى هذه القمم. إذاً، لم يعد هذا هدفاً متاحاً. وإذا ربطت هذا بالفيديو الخاص بي حول أحجام الذيول وا

ذا؟ يجب أن يكون لدينا نطاق يتجاوز ذلك المتوسط للوصول إلى هذه القمم. إذاً، لم يعد هذا هدفاً متاحاً. وإذا ربطت هذا بالفيديو الخاص بي حول أحجام الذيول والانعكاسات، فعند حدوث حركة معاكسة كبيرة كهذه، لا يعني ذلك أن السعر لا يمكنه الانعكاس والاستمرار في الارتفاع، لكنني الآن أغير توقعاتي. وهذا يتعلق بمتوسط النطاق اليومي. الآن، مع نفس متوسط النطاق اليومي هذا، ما هو الهدف الجيد؟ حسناً، 400 موجودة تماماً عند تلك النقطة. لدينا أعلى سعر لليوم السابق هنا، بالإضافة إلى احتمالية الوصول لهذه القمة، لكن هذا هو هدفنا الآن بينما نبحث عن ذلك الانعكاس ذي الفتيل الطويل. لو كنا قد توسعنا للتو، لكانت هناك فرصة للعودة إلى هنا، لكننا الآن نستهلك وقتاً طويلاً جداً. إذن، ماذا نلاحظ ؟ نحن نصعد ونصل هنا إلى هذه القمة السابقة . نعم، الشمعة أغلقت هنا، ولكن حتى لو كان لدينا المزيد من الوقت في اليوم، فهذا ليس شيئاً أتطلع لتداوله في اتجاه صاعد في هذا اليوم بالتحديد، لأننا استنفدنا معظم متوسط نطاقنا اليومي هنا وتجاوزنا أعلى سعر لليوم السابق. وهذا ما أوضحته في المثال مع ذلك الانعكاس ذي الفتيل الطويل. هذا هو الوقت الذي يكون فيه من الأفضل انتظار شمعة جديدة أو افتتاح يومي ج

ى سعر لليوم السابق. وهذا ما أوضحته في المثال مع ذلك الانعكاس ذي الفتيل الطويل. هذا هو الوقت الذي يكون فيه من الأفضل انتظار شمعة جديدة أو افتتاح يومي جديد للبحث عن نطاق جديد. إذن، ها نحن في مثال آخر. يمكنك رؤية الرسم البياني اليومي الخاص بنا هنا على اليمين. سأقوم بتنظيف هذه الرسومات الصعودية الموجودة عليه، ولكن دعونا نلقي نظرة على متوسط نطاقنا اليومي. حول ماذا يدور ؟ 116. إذن، إذا استطعنا رؤية السعر يستمر في الهبوط من هذه المنطقة ، أليس كذلك؟ وسنقوم أيضاً بتفعيل هذه الشمعة هنا حتى نتمكن من رؤية ذلك. يمكننا توقع وصول السعر إلى حوالي 115 نقطة. إذن، إذا كان لدينا فتيل صغير يحترم هذه النقطة ، يمكننا الحصول على توسع هبوطي، أليس كذلك ؟ ما الذي يوجد حول 115؟ هنا تماماً، عند هذه القيعان. إذن، إذا كان لدينا فتيل صغير، فلدينا هدف رائع هنا للوصول إليه. الآن، دعونا نرى ما سيحدث. بينما نترك الأمر يستمر، ما الذي تلاحظ حدوثه؟ نحن نقضي كل وقتنا داخل النطاق لتشكيل فتيل أكبر. إذن ، ماذا يفعل ذلك فيما يتعلق بنطاقنا اليومي ؟ إذا كانت هذه هي القمة، فأين يقع خط الـ 115 الخاص بنا؟ أليس كذلك؟ تماماً عند قاع اليوم السابق، وليس في الأسفل هنا. إذن، يمكنك رؤية كي

بنطاقنا اليومي ؟ إذا كانت هذه هي القمة، فأين يقع خط الـ 115 الخاص بنا؟ أليس كذلك؟ تماماً عند قاع اليوم السابق، وليس في الأسفل هنا. إذن، يمكنك رؤية كيف لدينا حركة معاكسة كبيرة، تستهلك الوقت داخل النطاق. الآن، لم يتبقَ لدينا الكثير من النطاق اليومي. إذن، هل أتطلع حقاً لأن يتوسع السعر إلى ما بعد قاع اليوم السابق هذا؟ لا، لأنه يكون قد استنفد معظم نطاقه اليومي بحلول الوقت الذي يصل فيه إلى هذه النقطة. إذن، نعم، يمكننا النظر إلى هذا كهدف، ولكن ليس حقاً إلا في اليوم التالي في معظم الأوقات. دعونا نرى ما سيحدث هنا. ويمكنك أن ترى أننا وصلنا إلى أدنى مستوى لليوم السابق. هل سنحصل على استمرار للاتجاه؟ لنرى. أليس كذلك؟ ليس قبل اليوم التالي. وهكذا يمكنك أن ترى كيف أن هذه الشمعة، لا نتوقع منها حقاً أن تتوسع بالكامل لأن لديها ذيلاً طويلاً. أنا لا أرغب في البحث عن استمرار أدنى من مستوى اليوم السابق هذا عندما لا يتبقى لدينا أي نطاق أو وقت في شمعة الإطار الزمني الأعلى هذه. إذاً، نحن هنا في هذا المثال التالي. ما الذي نلاحظه بخصوص متوسط النطاق اليومي هذا؟ إنه يتراوح تماماً حول علامة 100 إلى 105. إذاً، هذا ما يمكننا توقعه. ودعونا نلقي نظرة على هذا المثال ال

. ما الذي نلاحظه بخصوص متوسط النطاق اليومي هذا؟ إنه يتراوح تماماً حول علامة 100 إلى 105. إذاً، هذا ما يمكننا توقعه. ودعونا نلقي نظرة على هذا المثال السريع هنا . نلاحظ، ماذا لدينا؟ أدنى مستوى لليوم السابق. تم تجاوزه. لماذا قد تظل تبحث عن استمرار في الانخفاض هنا؟ لأن انظر إلى النطاق. لقد قطعنا 50. هذا نصف النطاق اليومي . ما الذي يمكننا الوصول إليه عند حدود 100؟ إذاً، من المنطقي البحث عن استمرار للاتجاه لأننا لم نستهلك كامل نطاقنا اليومي. إذاً، وبالنظر إلى هذا المثال الحالي ، نطاقنا اليومي حول علامة 105، لنرَ كيف سيتشكل هذا لأنه إذا تجاوزنا أعلى مستوى لليوم السابق، فلن يتبقى الكثير من النطاق. إذاً، هل لدينا ذيل صغير، مع بقاء جزء من متوسط النطاق اليومي (ADR) يمكننا التداول فيه صعوداً؟ أم أننا نقضي معظم وقتنا داخل النطاق لتشكيل ذلك الذيل حيث يصبح أعلى مستوى لليوم السابق هو هدفنا ولا نتطلع للتداول إلى ما بعده. وهنا يمكنك أن ترى أننا نتجاوز ذلك المستوى المرتفع على الفور، ولكن لا يزال بإمكاننا البحث عن استمرار طالما أن الدعم موجود لأن لدينا ذلك النطاق. وتلاحظ، ماذا لدينا؟ نصل إلى 105 ، ونحقق أهدافنا. الآن لا نبحث عن استمرار للاتجاه لأننا استن

لبحث عن استمرار طالما أن الدعم موجود لأن لدينا ذلك النطاق. وتلاحظ، ماذا لدينا؟ نصل إلى 105 ، ونحقق أهدافنا. الآن لا نبحث عن استمرار للاتجاه لأننا استنفدنا نطاقنا اليومي بالكامل. من الجيد البحث عن استمرار فوق أعلى مستوى لليوم السابق هنا لأن لدينا نطاقاً يومياً وأهدافاً مفتوحة لم تتحقق بعد. الآن، آمل أن يكون هذا الفيديو مفهوماً. عليك أن تمزجه بمنطق حجم الذيل والانعكاسات، بالإضافة إلى فهم مستويات الفتح والإغلاق وأعلى وأدنى سعر. ولكن، إذا كان لديك أي أسئلة، يرجى إخباري في قسم التعليقات أدناه. مع ذلك، أتمنى أن تكونوا قد استفدتم، وسأراكم في المرة القادمة. أتمنى لكم يوماً سعيداً.

A dealing range is the overall range you are trading within or toward.
Within the TTrades Fractal Model, the fractal gives you the setup. The dealing range gives you the range around that setup.
Find the swing point you are trading away from, find the higher timeframe swing that created it, and mark the range.
From there, use premium, discount, and EQ to position the trade and measure the available risk reward.

A dealing range is the range between the swing point you are trading away from and the higher timeframe swing you are trading toward.
For a bullish range, start with the low you are trading away from. Find the higher timeframe swing high that made that low and mark the range.
For a bearish range, start with the high you are trading away from. Find the higher timeframe swing low that made that high and mark the range.
That is the dealing range.

Start with a valid fractal model.
If you have a Candle 2 closure and are looking to trade Candle 3 higher, start with the Candle 2 low.
Move to the higher timeframe and find the swing high that made that low.
It will not always be Candle 1. Keep moving through the higher timeframe until you find the swing high.
Mark the high to the low.
That is your bullish dealing range.

The bearish range works the same way.
Start with a valid fractal model and find the high you are trading away from.
Move to the higher timeframe and find the swing low that made that high.
Mark the high to the low.
That is your bearish dealing range.

Split the dealing range at 50%.
The upper half is premium.
The lower half is discount.
EQ sits in the middle.
For bullish setups, look for longs in discount or around EQ.
For bearish setups, look for shorts in premium or around EQ.
The goal is simple. Enter with enough range between the entry and the target to reach your risk reward.

If you are long from discount, you have more range between your entry and the dealing range high.
If you are long from premium, you are already closer to the target.
The same applies to shorts.
A short in premium has more range toward the dealing range low. A short deep in discount is already closer to the target.
The setup can still work from a poor location. The issue is how much range is left for the trade.

Dealing ranges can form on every timeframe.
You can have a daily dealing range, an hourly dealing range, and another dealing range on the 15 minute or 5 minute.
The process stays the same.
Find the swing point you are trading away from. Find the swing that created it. Mark the range. Then use premium, discount, and EQ.

chunks.h: Using Dealing Ranges To Avoid Poor Entries
chunks.t:
A bearish setup deep in discount may still work, but the target is already close.
A bullish setup high in premium has the same problem.
Price can continue, but there may not be enough range for the risk reward you want.
The dealing range gives you a mechanical way to see how much room is left before entering.

The dealing range high is the target for a bullish range.
The dealing range low is the target for a bearish range.
Use that target to measure the available risk reward before entering.
Once the first target is taken, runners can continue toward the dealing range target.

Multiple dealing ranges can overlap.
A lower timeframe setup can form inside a higher timeframe dealing range.
For example, a short can form in premium of both the 5 minute and higher timeframe dealing ranges.
Now the entry is positioned within both ranges.
The same process applies to bullish setups.

Start with the fractal model.
Find the swing point you are trading away from. Find the higher timeframe swing that created it. Mark the range.
Then split it at EQ.
Look for longs in discount or around EQ. Look for shorts in premium or around EQ.
Use the dealing range target to measure the available risk reward.
That is the dealing range.

The fractal model gives you the setup.
The dealing range gives you the range.
Use premium, discount, and EQ to position the trade.
Then use the dealing range target to measure the risk reward.
Keep it mechanical.

القاع المتأرجح. إذن، دعونا نرى ما سيحدث. كما ترون، نحصل بالفعل على حركة هبوطية. ويمكنك رؤية كيف أن الإعداد هنا، من الناحية المثالية يجب أن يكون أعلى في منطقة متميزة، لكن هذا الإعداد هنا سيوفر مخاطرة إلى عائد أفضل من ذلك الموجود في منطقة الخصم. لأنه هنا ، إذا كنت سأحاول البيع على المكشوف، يمكنك أن ترى أنني لا أحصل حقاً على ضعف المخاطرة، أليس كذلك؟ بينما إذا قمت بالبيع على المكشوف في مكان ما عند إغلاق هذه الشمعة بالقرب من مستوى التعادل (EQ)، فيمكنني الآن الحصول على مخاطرة إلى عائد جيدة بما يكفي للتداول هبوطاً. في ملف الـ PDF الخاص بي، كان المثال متطرفاً بعض الشيء، لكنني أريد البيع على المكشوف في منطقة متميزة حول مستوى التعادل، حتى أتمكن من الحصول على مخاطرة إلى عائد جيدة. عندما أصل إلى 25%من النطاق أو أقل ، فهذا هو المكان الذي لا أبحث فيه حقاً عن صفقات بيع لأنها ليست مثالية من حيث المخاطرة إلى العائد. لذا، وبالمثل، دعونا نعود إلى هنا ونقوم بتنفيذ مثال آخر. هنا لدينا قاع متأرجح، عند إغلاق الشمعة، أين هي القمة المتأرجحة التي شكلته؟ هنا مباشرة. يمكننا المضي قدماً وتحديد نطاق التداول هذا. أين أرغب في البحث عن صفقات شراء؟ حول أو في منطقة ال

الشمعة، أين هي القمة المتأرجحة التي شكلته؟ هنا مباشرة. يمكننا المضي قدماً وتحديد نطاق التداول هذا. أين أرغب في البحث عن صفقات شراء؟ حول أو في منطقة الخصم. إذا قمت بالشراء هنا، فهذا يسمح لي بالحصول على مخاطرة إلى عائد جيدة مستهدفاً هذه القمم المتأرجحة الفاشلة. وبالمثل، يمكنك رؤية هذا التراجع مرة أخرى إلى منطقة الخصم في نطاق التداول، مما يهيئ الفرصة ويعطيني حركة محتملة للأعلى. صحيح، لذا يمكنني البحث عن إعدادات شراء حول مستوى التعادل أو في منطقة الخصم. أين لا أرغب في البحث عن صفقات شراء؟ حسناً، عندما أصبح مرتفعاً جداً أو في منطقة متميزة من هذا النطاق، أليس كذلك؟ لأنه الآن لا توجد مخاطرة إلى عائد كبيرة من حيث استهداف هذه القمم. وأحياناً لا يصل السعر ببساطة إلى تلك القمم، أليس كذلك؟ إنه يتوطد أو يشكل نوعاً من الانعكاس. لذا، أريد أن أتطلع للشراء في منطقة الخصم أو أسفل مستوى التعادل حولها. وأريد البيع على المكشوف في منطقة متميزة. إذن، دعونا ننتقل إلى مثال آخر. يمكنك أن ترى أن لدينا قمة متأرجحة. أين هو القاع المتأرجح؟ هذا الموجود هنا. لذا، سأحدد من تلك القمة إلى هذا القاع. وأين يكون من المثالي البيع على المكشوف؟ من الناحية المثالية، أريد البي

أين هو القاع المتأرجح؟ هذا الموجود هنا. لذا، سأحدد من تلك القمة إلى هذا القاع. وأين يكون من المثالي البيع على المكشوف؟ من الناحية المثالية، أريد البيع على المكشوف عند قمة هذا النطاق، أليس كذلك؟ لذا، من الناحية المثالية، ستكون صفقات البيع الخاصة بي هنا في الأعلى، أليس كذلك؟ هذا هو المكان الذي أريد أن أتطلع فيه إلى البيع. هل ترى كيف تقع كل هذه في منطقة متميزة من هذا النطاق، مما يمنح مخاطرة مقابل عائد جيدة لهذه الأهداف. الآن، نعم لدينا إعداد هبوطي هنا لاستمرار الحركة، ولكن هل هو مثالي؟ لا، لأنني لا أحصل على مخاطرة مقابل عائد جيدة بما يكفي. الآن، هناك شيء واحد أريد التحدث عنه في هذا المثال وهو أنه سيكون هناك نطاقات تداول متعددة داخل نطاقات أخرى. إذاً، هنا يمكنك رؤية أن لدينا نطاق التداول اليومي هذا، أليس كذلك ؟ أو على هذا الرسم البياني للساعة. ولكن، إذا انتقلنا إلى هذا الإطار الزمني الأدنى هنا، فما الذي سيكون لدينا؟ حسناً، الآن لدينا إعداد جديد هنا، ولكن على الرسم البياني للساعة و 5 دقائق. إذاً، أين سيكون نطاق التداول لإطار الـ 5 دقائق؟ من هذه القمة إلى هذه القاع. لذا، من الناحية المثالية على الرسم البياني لـ 5 دقائق، أريد البيع فوق أو ح

إذاً، أين سيكون نطاق التداول لإطار الـ 5 دقائق؟ من هذه القمة إلى هذه القاع. لذا، من الناحية المثالية على الرسم البياني لـ 5 دقائق، أريد البيع فوق أو حول مستوى التعادل ( EQ) هنا لأن ذلك سيمنحني مخاطرة مقابل عائد جيدة نحو هذا الهدف. إذاً، كيف تحصل على مخاطرة مقابل عائد جيدة حقاً؟ أنت تستخدم نطاقات تداول متعددة وتبيع في المنطقة المتميزة لكليهما. يمكنك رؤية أنه إذا كنت سأقوم بصفقة بيع في المنطقة المتميزة لنطاق التداول هذا على إطار 5 دقائق، وأنا أيضاً في المنطقة المتميزة لنطاق التداول اليومي والساعي، فهذا هو المكان الذي سأحصل فيه على مخاطرة مقابل عائد جيدة جداً لتلك الأهداف. ويمكنك رؤية كيف ينجح ذلك هناك. ستكون هناك أوقات يكون لديك فيها نطاقات تداول متداخلة. سيكون هناك بعض التفاصيل الدقيقة، ولكن من الناحية الميكانيكية هذه هي الطريقة التي أنظر بها إلى نطاقات التداول وأماكن التمركز. على سبيل المثال، إذا قمنا بالتكبير هنا إلى إطار الـ 5 دقائق، فأنا أريد البيع في المنطقة المتميزة من هذا النطاق. إذاً، يمكنك رؤية أين يحدث ذلك؟ هنا بالضبط. يمكنني أخذ أي نوع من الدخول أو إعادة الاختبار هنا . أضع وقف الخسارة عند تلك القمة المحمية. وبعد ذلك ما الذي

ذاً، يمكنك رؤية أين يحدث ذلك؟ هنا بالضبط. يمكنني أخذ أي نوع من الدخول أو إعادة الاختبار هنا . أضع وقف الخسارة عند تلك القمة المحمية. وبعد ذلك ما الذي يمكنني استهدافه؟ يمكنني الاستهداف والحصول على 2R عند ذلك الهدف الأول، وهذا ما أعنيه بمخاطرة مقابل عائد. أنت تحصل على مخاطرة مقابل عائد جيدة بما يكفي عند البيع حول مستوى التعادل أو في المنطقة المتميزة لهذا النطاق لتتمكن من جني الأرباح هنا، ولكن يمكنك الاحتفاظ بصفقاتك المتبقية حتى هدف نطاق التداول الآخر، وهذه هي الطريقة التي تحصل بها على مخاطرة مقابل عائد جيدة حقاً. الآن، نسبة المخاطرة إلى العائد ليست جيدة إذا كنت تحاول تداول هذه الاستمراريات، لنقل، هنا، لأن أين تتطلع أن تستهدف؟ هذا هو هدفك الأول. أنت لا تحصل حتى على نسبة واحد إلى واحد. هذه حالة، هل يمكنك القيام بها؟ بالتأكيد، هي ليست مثالية، لكن عليك حينها استهداف المزيد للحصول على تلك المخاطرة والعائد الجيدين. لذا، مع ذلك، أعتقد أن هذا مثال نهائي رائع للختام. إذا كان لديك أي ارتباك، أعد المشاهدة ، انضم إلى ديسكورد الخاص بي، اسأل في التعليقات، وسأرد عليكم في أقرب وقت ممكن. أتمنى لكم يوماً طيباً. أراكم في المرة القادمة.

If you are trading EURUSD or GBPUSD, you are naturally watching the dollar. But knowing whether the dollar is bullish or bearish is only half of the equation. The real edge comes from understanding which foreign currency is stronger or weaker. That is where EURGBP becomes a powerful relative strength tool.
In this guide, we are going to walk through exactly how to use EURGBP to determine whether you should be trading euro or pound when the dollar gives you directional bias.

chunks.h: Why Relative Strength Is So Important
chunks.t:
When the dollar is moving with strength, you want to pair it against yourself the weakest foreign currency. When the dollar is weak, you want to pair it against the strongest foreign currency.
Many traders get the dollar direction correct but choose the wrong pair. That usually results in slower moves, choppy price action, or missed expansion.
Relative strength fixes that.
EURGBP allows you to directly compare euro and pound to see which one is currently outperforming.

- Because both the Euro and the British Pound are quote-driven currencies paired against the US Dollar, their relative strength against each other can be measured using the EURGBP cross-rate.
- By analyzing EURGBP, a trader can determine which currency is fundamentally stronger or weaker at that moment, helping them decide whether to focus on trading EURUSD or GBPUSD.

Think of EURGBP as a fraction.
EUR over GBP.
If EURGBP is trending higher, that means euro is stronger than pound.If EURGBP is trending lower, that means euro is weaker than pound.
That simple relationship gives you clarity when choosing between EURUSD and GBPUSD.
You are no longer guessing. You are aligning with strength and weakness.

3. WHAT IT TEACHES:
This diagram teaches how to use the EUR/GBP intermarket relationship alongside the US Dollar Index (DXY) to determine relative currency strength and choose which currency pair (EUR/USD or GBP/USD) to trade. 

- When EUR/GBP is bullish, EUR is stronger than GBP. In this scenario, if the Dollar is bearish ($\text{DXY} \searrow$), you should buy the stronger currency against the dollar (Long EURUSD). If the Dollar is bullish ($\text{DXY} \nearrow$), you should sell the weaker currency against the dollar (Short GBPUSD).
- When EUR/GBP is bearish, EUR is weaker than GBP. In this scenario, if the Dollar is bearish ($\text{DXY} \searrow$), you should buy the stronger currency against the dollar (Long GBPUSD). If the Dollar is bullish ($\text{DXY} \nearrow$), you should sell the weaker currency against the dollar (Short EURUSD).

chunks.t:
If the dollar is trending higher or expanding with strong daily closes, you want to be shorting foreign currencies.
Now you check EURGBP.
If EURGBP is bullish, euro is stronger and pound is weaker. In that case, you focus on shorting GBPUSD because you are pairing strong dollar with weak pound.
If EURGBP is bearish, euro is weaker and pound is stronger. In that case, you focus on shorting EURUSD because euro is the weaker currency.
The goal is simple. Pair strength against weakness.

If the dollar is trading lower and showing expansion to the downside, you want to be buying foreign currencies.
Again, check EURGBP.
If EURGBP is bullish, euro is stronger. You would focus on longing EURUSD.
If EURGBP is bearish, pound is stronger. You would focus on longing GBPUSD.
In both cases, you are pairing weak dollar with the strongest foreign currency available.
That combination often produces the cleanest trends and strongest daily expansion.

chunks.h: Using Daily Candle Closures for Confirmation
chunks.t:
Beyond just trend direction on EURGBP, you can compare daily candle closures between EURUSD and GBPUSD.
Look for:
Strong body closuresBreaks of prior highs or lowsEngulfing candlesClear displacement
If GBPUSD is closing aggressively lower while EURUSD is holding structure better, that confirms pound is weaker.
If EURUSD is breaking structure while GBPUSD is holding firm, that confirms euro is weaker.
You do not need complex indicators. Structure and candle behavior are enough.

note: **SUMMARY**  
The lesson teaches how to use EURGBP as a relative‑strength tool to decide whether to trade EURUSD or GBPUSD when the dollar gives a directional bias. By observing the trend of EURGBP, you pair the strongest foreign currency against the weakest relative to the dollar’s direction, improving trade alignment with momentum. This approach reduces choppy action and missed expansion, making dollar‑based trades more precise.  
**KEY RULES**  
- If the dollar is bullish (trending higher or expanding with strong daily closes), **short the weaker foreign currency**.  
- If the dollar is bearish (trading lower and expanding to the downside), **long the stronger foreign currency**.  
- Use EURGBP to determine which foreign currency is stronger or weaker.  
- When EURGBP is bullish, euro is stronger and pound is weaker.  
- When EURGBP is bearish, euro is weaker and pound is stronger.  
- With a bullish dollar, short GBPUSD when EURGBP is bullish; short EURUSD when EURGBP is bearish.  
- With a bearish dollar, long EURUSD when EURGBP is bullish; long GBPUSD when EURGBP is bearish.  
- Confirm EURGBP trend with daily candle closures of EURUSD and GBPUSD:  
  - Strong body closures, breaks of prior highs/lows, engulfing candles, clear displacement.

note:   - If GBPUSD closes aggressively lower while EURUSD holds structure, pound is weaker.  
  - If EURUSD breaks structure while GBPUSD holds firm, euro is weaker.  
**DEFINITIONS**  
- **EURGBP** – the currency pair representing euro over pound; used as a fraction to gauge relative strength.  
- **Bullish trend** – EURGBP trending higher, indicating euro stronger than pound.  
- **Bearish trend** – EURGBP trending lower, indicating euro weaker than pound.  
- **Dollar bullish** – dollar trending higher or expanding with strong daily closes.  
- **Dollar bearish** – dollar trading lower and expanding to the downside.  
**MISTAKES / INVALIDATION**  
- The lesson does not provide a standalone trade setup; it is only a decision‑making tool for pair selection.  
- Do not rely on complex indicators; structure and candle behavior are sufficient for confirmation.

If you trade forex and want more consistent expansion moves, understanding how to pair currencies using futures can completely change your framework.
This approach is rooted in something surprisingly simple: fractions.
Every forex pair is essentially a fraction. Once you understand how the numerator and denominator behave mathematically, you can identify which currency combinations are most likely to produce strong trends and which ones to avoid.
Let’s break it down step by step.

chunks.h: The Fraction Concept Behind Currency Pairs
chunks.t:
Every forex pair works like this:
Currency / Currency
For example, EUR/USD represents Euro over US Dollar, and USD/JPY represents US Dollar over Japanese Yen.
Think of it as starting with 1 over 1 equaling 1, which represents neutrality.
Now here is where the math matters.
If you raise the denominator, the value of the fraction decreases.If you lower the numerator, the value of the fraction decreases.If you raise the numerator and lower the denominator, the value increases strongly.If you lower the numerator and raise the denominator, the value decreases strongly.
Translated into currencies, a strong currency paired with a weak creates a bullish pair. A weak currency paired with a strong creates a bearish pair.
This is the foundation of currency pairing.

chunks.h: What to Avoid When Pairing Currencies
chunks.t:
Not all combinations create strong moves. Some combinations cancel each other out.
You want to avoid pairing a strong currency with another strong currency. You also want to avoid pairing a weak currency with another weak currency.
When both currencies are moving in the same direction, the pair often consolidates instead of expanding.
For example, if both USD and EUR are strong, trading EUR/USD may produce choppy price action instead of a clean trend.
You want opposites, not similarities.

chunks.h: The Golden Rule Strongest Versus Weakest
chunks.t:
The most powerful moves happen when you pair the strongest currency with the weakest currency.
If USD is very bullish and EUR is very bearish, trading EUR/USD can produce strong downside expansion.
If USD is bearish and JPY is bullish, trading USD/JPY can produce strong downside expansion.
Opposites create momentum. That is the key idea.

chunks.h: Using the Dollar Index as Your Anchor
chunks.t:
The US Dollar Index, often referred to as DXY, measures overall dollar strength.
Start your analysis here.
If DXY is trending higher, the dollar is strong. In that case, you want to pair it with the weakest available currency.
If DXY is trending lower, the dollar is weak. In that case, you want to pair it with the strongest available currency.
If DXY is consolidating, the approach changes.

chunks.h: What to Do When the Dollar Is Consolidating
chunks.t:
When the dollar is ranging, you do not need to focus on USD pairs at all. Instead, look for a strong foreign currency and a weak foreign currency and pair them together.
For example, If GBP is bearish and NZD is bullish, you could look at GBP/NZD.
When the dollar is flat, cross pairs often provide cleaner expansion than USD pairs.

If you trade currency futures instead of forex, the logic is the same.
If the dollar is bullish, trade the most bearish currency future.
If the dollar is bearish, trade the most bullish currency future.
If the dollar is consolidating, you can either trade the strongest single future or go long one strong future and short one weak future. That structure mimics trading a cross pair such as EUR/JPY.
The math remains identical because the relationship between currencies does not change.

Start by checking the trend of the US Dollar Index.
Then rank currency futures by strength and weakness.
Avoid pairing currencies that are moving in the same direction.
Focus on pairing the strongest with the weakest.
Accept that some days will offer multiple good options, while other days will require patience.
Your goal is not to predict everything. Your goal is to align with relative strength.

This framework can feel advanced at first, but it becomes intuitive with repetition.
- Understand fractions.
- Pair opposites.
- Avoid similarities.
- Start with the dollar.
Once you begin thinking in terms of relative strength instead of isolated charts, your pair selection becomes far more intentional.
And that is where expansion lives.

The “Power of 3” is one of the most effective ways to trade higher timeframe candles, especially on the 4-hour chart. At its core, it follows the AMD model: accumulation, manipulation, and distribution. When applied to 4-hour candles, this model helps identify whether price is building up, running stops, or expanding in the true direction. In this guide, we’ll break down how to read 4-hour candles using the open, high, low, and close, and how to use lower timeframes to time entries more effectively.

  - Phase 2 (Manipulation): Highlighted by a red/pink shaded vertical zone immediately following the accumulation phase. It features sharp downward-moving black candles breaking below the accumulation range (a false breakdown/sweep of liquidity), labeled with an arrow pointing to "Manipulation".

3. WHAT IT TEACHES:
- PO3 stands for "Power of Three," a core concept (often associated with ICT/Smart Money Concepts) describing how market makers and institutional smart money engineer liquidity before executing their true intended move.
- The model teaches a three-step cycle:
  1. **Accumulation:** Smart money builds positions or allows retail traders to trap themselves within a consolidation range.
  2. **Manipulation:** Price sharply moves in one direction (often breaking a key support or resistance level) to trigger stop losses and trap breakout traders, creating liquidity.
  3. **Distribution:** Once the liquidity is grabbed, price rapidly reverses and impulses heavily in the true institutional direction (in this bullish example, shooting upward).

The Power of 3 is built on three phases:
- Accumulation: a range where price builds liquidity.
- Manipulation: a false move against the intended direction.
- Distribution: the true expansion or directional move.
When looking at a 4-hour candle, the first candle in sequence is accumulation. Candle two often shows manipulation, and candle three tends to deliver the expansion. However, sometimes manipulation and distribution happen within the same candle. The trick is recognizing whether the wick that forms early in the candle supports expansion or not.

If candle two has a large opposing run — meaning price makes a deep move against your bias — it usually does not support expansion within that candle. Instead, you wait for candle three to deliver the move.If candle two has only a shallow wick, that wick can serve as manipulation and the body can become the expansion. In this case, you can trade within the same 4-hour candle.
The goal is to wait for the wick to form, confirm it as a protected swing, and then trade in the direction of the body. Trying to catch the wick itself often leads to stop-outs.

To trade a 4-hour power of 3 effectively, you need to drill down to lower timeframes. The 15-minute chart pairs well with the 4-hour for entry confirmation. For futures, key times like 2am, 6am and 10am often serve as anchors for reversals and continuations. In forex, the 1am, 5am, 9am sessions are more relevant.
On the lower timeframe, look for:
- A reach into a point of interest.
- A change in the state of delivery (CISD) to confirm a protected swing.
- Continuation entries after the wick has formed.
This approach allows you to align your trades with the expansion phase of the 4-hour candle.

chunks.t:
Most traders look for breakers at market reversals, where a trend shifts from bearish to bullish or vice versa.
For continuation trading, the process is slightly different:
Identify the trend
- Confirm bias from higher timeframes using structure and protected swings.
Wait for a liquidity sweep
- A swing low sweep in an uptrend (or swing high sweep in a downtrend) is necessary to form the breaker.
Confirm with structure
- After the sweep, the breaker block forms only once price makes a higher high (in bullish cases) or lower low (in bearish cases).
Execute on retests
- Entries can be taken on the breaker block retest, with stops placed beyond the opposite side of the block.
Pro Tip: Focus on breaker blocks that have a strong close over the high (bullish) or strong close below their low (bearish)

In trading, many traders feel they’ve missed their chance if they don’t catch the very first reversal entry. That’s not the case. Once a reversal is confirmed, it often opens the door for continuation entries, structured opportunities to enter with better confirmation and, often, improved risk-to-reward. This guide breaks down how I use order blocks to capture those continuations.

Before looking for continuations, you must confirm a reversal sequence.
For example:
- Purge (liquidity sweep)
- Change in the State of Delivery (CISD) sets your invalidation point.
- Initial entry may come from an order block at this point.
If you miss that entry or prefer more confirmation, wait for structure to form, essentially a higher low in an uptrend or a lower high in a downtrend.

For continuations, I focus on:
Fair Value Gaps (FVGs)
- Price retraces into a FVG followed by a CISD.
Swept Lows/Highs
- Liquidity sweep followed by a CISD.
Correlated Asset SMT Divergence
- If one correlated asset sweeps a level but the other doesn’t, I can still classify the setup as valid.
💡 Pro Tip: Continuation OBs formed from a fair value gap or from sweeping a low are Protected Swings.

After price reaches a point of interest:
- Wait for a closure through the opposing candles (up-close in a short bias, down-close in a long bias).
- This closure validates the order block and sets your stop placement.
💡 Pro Tip: Always use the series of candles. Only use the single candle if there are no other opposing candles.

chunks.t:
Daily Context: Following an aggressive bearish expansion, price has a retracement into a bearish fair value gap where it then consolidates. Upon the sweep of the consolidation high, there is a bearish daily closure.
Intraday Sequence:
1. Mark out the lower half (EQ) of the daily candle, this is the area we want to see price respect. Due to the unfavorable close of the daily candle, we will allow price to trade a little higher into the range – we just want the daily candle to have a small wick.
2. Price then has a bearish closure on the hourly chart.
3. Dropping to the 5-minute chart, wait for the CISD forming a protected high
4. Seeking a continuation in the next hourly candle, it is not clean with the consolidation higher into the range. When this occurs, allow for displacement and the market to tell you where it wants to go.
5. Following the displacement lower, continue tracking the protected swings and find a continuation order block for entry lower

💡 Pro Tip: Look to target the daily or hourly levels for higher R:R. The 2R trade above becomes 7R when reaching for the previous day low daily target. Even 10R+ when holding until end of day close. Expansion candles tend to close near the high or low of the candle.

- Aggressive Displacement: In large moves, I often look for retest entries rather than entering immediately. This allows for good R:R
- Grinding Moves: If price trends without sweeping lows/highs or hitting FVGs, I pass on the trade.
- Fractal: The same continuation logic works on all timeframes, from 1-minute to monthly.

- Missing the reversal isn’t the end, you can trade continuations with clear structure.
- Look for price to return to a FVG or sweep liquidity before forming an order block.
- Confirmation comes from the closure through the opposing candles in your point of interest.
- Apply this approach across all timeframes, it is fractal.
- The goal is a repeatable, mechanical process, avoid chasing price and focus on setups that meet your defined criteria.

chunks.t:
Internal range liquidity is represented by fair value gaps (FVGs) within a range.
- A bullish FVG shows an imbalance where price moved aggressively higher.
- A bearish FVG highlights inefficiency where price moved aggressively lower.
💡 Pro Tip: Look for a higher low or a lower high to be formed within fair value gaps as a continuation of a trend.

chunks.t:
External range liquidity is simply swing points : swing highs and swing lows.
- A sweep of a swing low represents a purge of sell-side liquidity
- A sweep of a swing high clears buy-side liquidity
These liquidity pools act as magnets for price, providing clear targets.

3. WHAT IT TEACHES:
- The rule demonstrated is that market liquidity runs in cycles between the outer boundaries of a dealing range and its interior.
- When price takes out External Range Liquidity (ERL)—such as old highs or lows (stops)—it has completed an objective on one end of the spectrum.
- Once ERL is purged, traders should anticipate a corrective or retracement move back into Internal Range Liquidity (IRL)—such as Fair Value Gaps, order blocks, or liquidity voids inside the range—before the next major continuation or expansion occurs.

Instead of guessing or reacting late, the Next Day Model (sometimes called the Next Candle Model) provides a structured way to anticipate price behavior using nothing more than the previous candle. This diagram teaches how to differentiate between a market continuation and a market reversal based on how a candle interacts with a previous candle's extreme (high or low):
- **Reversal:** When a candle sweeps a key level (the high or low of the previous candle) but fails to sustain momentum and closes in the opposite direction, it signals a reversal.
- **Continuation:** When a candle sweeps a key level (the high or low of the previous candle) and continues pushing strongly in that same direction, it signals a continuation of the trend.

chunks.t:
The foundation of the Next Day Model is the relationship between a candle and its previous high or low:
- Reversal: Price sweeps the previous candle’s high or low, then closes back inside the range.Example: If yesterday’s high is swept, but the candle closes back inside, it signals potential bearish continuation the next day.
- Continuation: Price sweeps the previous candle’s high or low, then closes outside the range.Example: If today closes above yesterday’s high, anticipate a bullish continuation the following day.
This simple framework allows traders to form a bias for the next candle without overcomplicating analysis.

chunks.h: Blending With Phases of Price Delivery
chunks.t:
Price doesn’t move in one straight line. Instead, it cycles through phases:
- Expansion
- Retracement
- Consolidation
- Reversal
When you recognize multiple days of expansion, it’s wise to expect a shift in phase. For example:
- After three consecutive bearish continuations, it is likely for price to enter a new phase of price : retracement, reversal, or consolidation.
Instead of forcing continuation trades after price has already expanded, wait for price to enter a new phase of price. This will keep traders from getting caught shorting the low or longing the high.

chunks.h: Practical Examples on the Daily Chart
chunks.t:
Looking at daily candles:
- A close outside the previous high → bias for continuation.
- A sweep and close back inside → bias for reversal.
- Multiple candles expanding in one direction → expect retracement, consolidation, or reversal soon.
For example:
- Sweep of a daily high, close back inside the range → anticipate bearish price action the next day.
- Closure below the previous candle low → anticipate bearish continuation.
Since the concept is fractal, you can scale it down to the hourly or even 5-minute charts.

chunks.h: Why This Works Well in Practice
chunks.t:
- It’s mechanical and repeatable, just track the previous candle closes.
- It works across all timeframes, making it versatile for swing traders and scalpers alike.

- A close outside the previous candle’s high or low = continuation bias.
- A sweep and close back inside = reversal bias.
- After multiple continuation candles, expect retracement or reversal.
- Use lower timeframes to refine entries once higher-timeframe bias is set.
The Next Day Model is a simple, yet powerful model that can be used for bias as well as lower timeframe entries.

The Seek and Destroy profile is one of those daily patterns that many traders prefer to avoid. It’s a setup that reflects market indecision and often results in frustrating, low-probability price action. However, understanding how it works is critical, not so much to trade it aggressively, but to recognize it and know when to step aside. In this blog, we’ll break down what a Seek and Destroy profile is, why it happens, and how to navigate it if you decide to engage.

chunks.h: What is a Seek and Destroy Profile?
chunks.t:
On the daily chart, a Seek and Destroy profile appears as an indecision candle, where price opens and closes around the same level, showing little to no clear direction.
On lower timeframes, this looks like:
- London session taking both the Asia high and Asia low without sustained breakout
- Price oscillating between range boundaries instead of expanding in one direction
- New York often following suit, producing consolidation instead of trend continuation
The price action this day is whipsaw-like, offering little net movement compared to directional days.

Two primary reasons tend to create Seek and Destroy conditions:
- High-impact news events approaching (for example CPI, FOMC, NFP). Markets wait for clarity
- Lack of higher timeframe direction, daily chart in indecision
These days often appear after strong expansion days, when the market needs to rebalance or consolidate before choosing direction again.

To spot these days early:
- Watch the Asia range and see how London behaves
- If London sweeps both Asia high and low with a lack of direction, it often signals consolidation conditions
- If London already creates most of the day’s range, New York has limited room to expand further
In both cases, expectations for trending conditions should be lowered.

Although many traders prefer to avoid this profile, the best approach is trading back into the range rather than chasing breakouts.
Key tactics include:
- Marking out equilibrium (50 percent level) of the London range and using this as a magnet for price returning inside the range
- Watching for false breakouts beyond Asia or London highs and lows, then fading them back toward the middle
- Using the daily open or Asia range as rebalancing points, since price tends to gravitate there
In short, you’re not trading for expansion, you’re trading consolidation. Expect price to continue to consolidate unless proven otherwise.
In one Nasdaq example, London swept both sides of Asia and New York simply mirrored the whipsaw back toward equilibrium and daily open

chunks.h: The Real Lesson: Knowing When to Stay Out
chunks.t:
Perhaps the most important takeaway is that Seek and Destroy conditions are low-probability. They don’t provide clean expansions, and traders seeking directional moves will often get chopped up.
Recognizing them allows you to:
- Conserve capital by avoiding poor conditions
- Save mental energy for high-probability setups
- Better anticipate when consolidation is likely, especially after large directional days

The Seek and Destroy profile isn’t about finding opportunity, it’s about recognizing non-opportunity. Successful traders know when not to trade, and this profile is a perfect example of when patience pays more than participation.

In trading, timing often matter just as much as the price an asset is trading. The Daily Profile framework helps traders understand how price tends to move within different sessions. One of the most straight forward setups is the New York manipulation profile, where the New York session sweeps the current days range high or low and then deliveries in the opposite direction.
This blog will break down what the New York manipulation profile looks like, how it plays out in bullish and bearish contexts, and how traders can frame entries using concepts like the change in the state of delivery.

chunks.h: What is the New York Manipulation Profile?
chunks.t:
The New York manipulation is the Open-High-Low-Close (bullish profile) or Open-Low-High-Close (bearish profile) structure of a daily candle.
- Bullish case: London consolidates, New York sweeps the range low, has a change in the state of delivery and then expands upward.
- Bearish case: London consolidates, New York sweeps the range high, has a change in the state of delivery and then expands downward.
This mirrors the Power of Three Model: Accumulation – Manipulation – Distribution.

chunks.h: How to Recognize It on Charts
chunks.t:
To spot a New York manipulation, traders typically look for:
- London Session Behavior: Did London create a significant high/low, or just consolidate? If it failed to reach a key level, New York is more likely to sweep the range high or low.
- Liquidity Sweeps: Around 8:30 AM or 9:30 AM (News release and NYSE open), watch for false moves that sweep liquidity above or below London’s range.
- Change in the State of Delivery: After the sweep, price must close through the opposing candles (e.g., down close candles in a bullish reversal) to confirm a directional shift.
- Entry Models: Traders can refine entries using fair value gaps (FVGs), order blocks (OBs), or their choice of an entry model

SUMMARY: The lesson explains how the New York manipulation profile—an Open‑High‑Low‑Close structure that sweeps the daily range and then reverses—appears in bullish and bearish contexts. It teaches traders to identify the setup by watching London consolidation, New York liquidity sweeps at 8:30 AM or 9:30 AM, and a change in the state of delivery before entering. Entry points are framed around order blocks or fair‑value gaps with stops below the low, and targets are usually the previous day’s high or low. The concept is part of the Power of Three model (Accumulation‑Manipulation‑Distribution).
KEY RULES  
- Identify London session behavior: consolidation or failure to reach a key level.  
- Watch for liquidity sweeps at 8:30 AM or 9:30 AM (news release, NYSE open).  
- Confirm a change in the state of delivery: price must close through the opposing candles (e.g., down‑close candles in a bullish reversal).  
- Refine entries with fair‑value gaps (FVGs) or order blocks (OBs).  
- Place stop below the low of the manipulation.  
- Target the previous day’s high (PDH) for bullish or previous day’s low (PDL) for bearish.  
- If 8:30 AM forms the manipulation, look for 9:30 AM or 10 AM to drive price in its intended direction.

SUMMARY: - Use confluences: Standard Deviation projections (2.0–2.5 lines up with PDH/PDL, 4.0–4.5 marks maximum expansion).  
- 4H Power of Three: if 9:30 AM forms the manipulation, look for the 10 AM 4H PO3.
DEFINITIONS  
- **New York manipulation profile**: The Open‑High‑Low‑Close (bullish) or Open‑Low‑High‑Close (bearish) structure of a daily candle where New York sweeps the range high or low and then expands in the opposite direction.  
- **State of delivery**: The directional bias of price action, confirmed when price closes through the opposing candles after a sweep.  
- **Fair‑value gap (FVG)**: A price area lacking trading volume, used as an entry zone.  
- **Order block (OB)**: A consolidation zone that can act as support or resistance.  
- **Previous Day’s High (PDH)**: The highest price of the prior trading day, used as a target.  
- **Previous Day’s Low (PDL)**: The lowest price of the prior trading day, used as a target.  
- **Killzones**: Time‑zone diagram showing market trading sessions in Eastern Standard Time (EST).  
- **Standard Deviation projections**: Lines (2.0–2.5, 4.0–4.5) used to identify expansion targets.
MISTAKES / INVALIDATION  
- Do not enter before confirming a change in the state of delivery.

SUMMARY: - Avoid trading if London has already set a clear high or low; New York is less likely to sweep the range.  
- Do not ignore liquidity sweeps; false moves can mislead if not recognized.

If you’ve been studying ICT concepts, you know how important the daily profile is when framing intraday setups. In part one of the series, London Reversal was the focus. This time, we’re diving into the New York Reversal, a powerful concept that often provides clean intraday setups when London fails to reach a higher time frame level.
The New York Reversal centers around price action that unfolds in the New York AM session, typically between 8:30–11:00 AM EST. By understanding its characteristics, traders can better identify where liquidity pools, higher time frame levels, and the change in the state of delivery (CISD) come together to create high-probability trades.

chunks.h: What is the New York Reversal?
chunks.t:
The New York Reversal occurs when:
- London session makes a retracement or expansion but does not reach a relevant higher time frame PD Array (Premium/Discount Array).
- Price extends further during New York’s AM session, reaching that higher time frame key level.
- Once that key level is engaged, a change in the state of delivery (CISD) confirms the shift, often leading to a strong opposing move.
Think of it this way:
- London Reversal: London session itself reaches the key level and reverses.
- New York Reversal: London falls short, leaving New York to complete the run into the key level before reversing.

chunks.h: Characteristics of a Bullish New York Reversal
chunks.t:
- London session trades lower but fails to hit a significant higher time frame support level.
- New York session continues that move down, hits the key level, then shifts structure.
- After the CISD, price aggressively rallies, often running through multiple liquidity highs.

chunks.h: Characteristics of a Bearish New York Reversal
chunks.t:
- London retraces higher but fails to engage a higher time frame resistance.
- New York session extends the rally, taps into the resistance, then shifts lower.
- After the CISD, price sells off, targeting lows and liquidity resting beneath.

When trading New York reversals, look for:
- Liquidity Pools: Equal highs/lows, failure swings, or session highs/lows.
- Higher Time Frame Levels: Previous day’s high/low, order blocks, or fair value gaps.
- Change in the State of Delivery (CISD): A clear displacement and closure past a series of opposing candles.
- Time Alignment: The best setups occur between 8:30 AM and 10:30 AM EST, when volatility aligns with New York’s open and major economic releases.

chunks.h: Example Flow of a New York Reversal Trade
chunks.t:
1. London Session: Price trades but does not hit a higher time frame PD array.
2. New York AM: Price sweeps liquidity into a higher time frame key level.
3. Confirmation: Wait for displacement and CISD on a 15M/5M chart.
4. Entry: Place entry after the close above/below the CISD level.
5. Stops & Targets:Stops: Below the low (for bullish) or above the high (for bearish).Targets: Failure swings, session highs/lows, or low-resistance liquidity pools.

The New York Reversal is one of the most consistent intraday setups when understood correctly. By combining daily profiles, liquidity, and change in state of delivery (CISD) traders can filter false moves and anticipate strong reversals.
Next time you study your charts, ask: Did London reach a significant PD array? If not, is New York likely to run into that level for the reversal?
Mastering this distinction can drastically improve trade selection and timing.

chunks.t:
The London Reversal is when London session creates the wick of the daily candle.
- Bullish London Reversal:Daily candle opens.London manipulates lower, creating the low of the day.A change in the state of delivery (CISD) confirms bullish delivery.New York session then forms a continuation of London’s reversal.
- Bearish London Reversal:
- Daily candle opens.London manipulates higher, creating the high of the day.A change in the state of delivery (CISD) confirms bearish delivery.New York session then forms a continuation of London’s reversal.

The role of the New York session is to trade the expansion following the reversal.
- After a London low (bullish setup), look for New York session to form continuations out of fair value gaps or sweeping out lows.
- After a London high (bearish setup), look for New York session to form continuations out of fair value gaps or sweeping out highs.
Common price action elements to look for:
- Order blocks formed by London’s shift.
- Fair value gaps (FVGs) offering retracement entries.
- Time-based confluence around 8:30, 9:30, and 10:00 AM EST.
💡 Pro Tip: Avoid New York session when London forms the reversal and the expansion. This is when the average daily range has already been completed and sets up unfavorable conditions for New York.

Lets look at some chart examples:
- On a bullish day, price opens and then during London session, sweeps out a low to its left, forms a CISD. Then during New York session, price continues in the direction of the daily candle, forming continuations which can be traded.

chunks.h: Why This Matters for Daily Candles
chunks.t:
When you step back to the daily chart, you’ll see how this behavior completes the OHLC structure:
- Daily wick = London session
- Body of daily candle = New York session
This pattern repeats often enough that it forms one of the core daily profiles.

- London session (2–5 AM EST) defines the daily wick through a small opposing run.
- A CISD during London confirms the reversal and profile.
- New York session (8:30–12 PM EST) provides continuation trades in alignment with London’s reversal.
- This process forms the daily candle’s open, high/low, and close structure.
Mastering this concept helps traders align intraday execution with the daily narrative.

chunks.t:
There are specific times during the trading day when new candles open on higher timeframes. These open-high-low-close (OHLC) structures give traders valuable insight into where liquidity and order flow may shift.
The main OHLC times to watch are:
- 18:00 EST – Daily candle open
- 02:00 EST – 4-hour candle open
- 06:00 EST – 4-hour candle open
- 10:00 EST – 4-hour candle open
- 14:00 EST – 4-hour candle open
How to use them:
- The goal is to let the wick of the daily candle form, thus I am focused on the opposing run from the daily open (18:00) creating that wick.
- Each 4-hour open (02:00, 06:00, 10:00, 14:00) provides an intraday structure. Look for the classic pattern: open → low → high → close (bullish) or open → high → low → close (bearish). This helps anticipate how the candle forms.
- Be sure to check out my dedicated video on OHLC for a full understanding of this concept.

chunks.h: Midnight and 8:30 as Support and Resistance
chunks.t:
Two additional time levels function less as OHLC structures and more as intraday support and resistance markers:
- Midnight (0:00) – The new calendar day open. Often acts as a key level that price will revisit, reject, or use as a pivot for the day’s direction.
- 08:30 EST – The release time for major U.S. economic data. Price frequently reacts sharply here, making it a strong reference for support/resistance zones.
In practice:
- If price trades above midnight and 8:30 levels in a bearish context, this can be viewed as deep premium or a favorable condition for shorting.
- If price trades below them in a bullish context, that’s a deep discount, an attractive area for long entries.

- Specifically, price drops below the **[0:00]** opening price to induce short sellers and trap liquidity (forming an Order Block), before reversing sharply around key time windows (**[8:30]** and **[9:30]**) to expand in the true direction of the day, resulting in a large directional daily candle.

chunks.t:
An opposing run occurs when the market makes an “opposing run” in the “wrong” direction before reversing into the real move. This often traps traders.
- 08:30 EST – News-driven volatility. Expect sudden sweeps of liquidity (highs or lows) before a move back into order flow.
- 09:30 EST – New York Stock Exchange open. A powerful moment where volatility increases. Often delivers another opposing run, either running stops above/below short-term levels before trending in the opposite direction. Price can also expand if the manipulation or the 8:30 opposing run already occurred.
💡 Pro Tip:
- 8:30 opposing run → 9:30 expansion.
- No opposing run at 8:30 → 9:30 opposing run. 9:30 / 10:00 expansion.
For example:
- In a bullish day, you might see 08:30 make a move lower then a sharp reversal higher.
- At 09:30, price may expand higher in line with the higher timeframe trend.

Here’s how a trader might structure their day using these time levels:
- Mark 0:00 and 8:30 as support/resistance reference points.
- Track OHLC at 18:00, 06:00, 10:00, 14:00, and 02:00 to anticipate intraday structure.
- Watch 08:30 and 09:30 for opposing runs.
By combining these elements, you create a powerful framework: time tells you when liquidity may be taken, OHLC gives you structure for price delivery, and runs provide invalidations.
💡 Pro Tip: Opposing runs create protected swings when reaching into a fair value gap or sweeping out a high (bearish) or low (bullish)

Trading is not just about price, it’s about when price makes its moves. By mastering the rhythm of OHLC levels, the power of midnight and 8:30 as support/resistance, and opposing runs at 8:30 and 9:30, you can align yourself with institutional timing and gain a sharper edge in the markets.

The MMXM Trader’s “Twitter Model” is an ICT-inspired trading framework designed to simplify how traders identify high-probability setups. At its core, the model blends liquidity raids, fair value gaps (FVGs), market structure shifts (MSS), and SMT divergences across multiple timeframes. What makes it powerful is its adaptability — it’s fractal, meaning it can be applied on any timeframe, depending on the market context.
Let’s break it down step by step so you can see how this strategy works in practice.

chunks.h: Core Concept of the Twitter Model
chunks.t:
The Twitter Model revolves around a liquidity raid → fair value gap → entry confirmation flow.
- Liquidity Raid: Identify where price sweeps the previous day’s high (for shorts) or low (for longs).
- Higher Timeframe FVG: After the sweep, locate a fair value gap on the 1-hour chart (bullish for shorts, bearish for longs).
- Entry Timeframe Confirmation: Drop to the 15-minute chart to find a market structure shift (MSS) and SMT divergence for entry refinement.
- Midnight Open Filter: Only take shorts above midnight open and longs below midnight open.
This framework ensures that entries align with institutional price delivery, not random intraday moves.

chunks.t:
Here’s how it typically plays out:
1. Daily Chart – Price runs previous day’s high → liquidity grab complete.
2. Hourly Chart – Identify a bullish FVG → target for a short.
3. 15-Minute Chart – Wait for MSS + SMT divergence. Example: Gold vs Silver or NQ vs ES.
4. Execution – Enter short above midnight open, stop behind the shift candle, target the hourly FVG.
This process ensures you’re trading with the draw on liquidity rather than against it.

- SMT : When two correlated assets behave differently. Example: ES makes a higher high while NQ makes a lower high. This hints at weakness.
- MSS : A clear break and close beyond a key swing point, signaling intent.
Both tools refine entries so you aren’t blindly entering after a liquidity sweep.

It teaches that what appears as a simple high or a single candle on a higher timeframe (like a Weekly candle) is actually a detailed sequence of price swings, liquidity grabs, and structural shifts on lower timeframes (like H4 and H1). Specifically, it shows how higher-timeframe key levels—such as a Previous Week High (PWH)—are tested on lower timeframes accompanied by confirming clues like SMT divergence and a Market Structure Shift (MSS) before executing a reversal or continuation model.

chunks.t:
One strength of this model is that it’s timeframe flexible:
- Daily → Hourly → 15m (standard setup)
- Weekly → 4H → 1H (higher timeframe swing trades)
- Hourly → 5m → 1m (scalping environments)
As long as you respect the same sequence — raid, FVG, MSS/SMT — the model remains valid.

The MMXM Trader also notes possible adjustments:
- Instead of midnight open, you can filter entries with daily open depending on market context.
- Instead of MSS, you may look for inversions or changes in the state of delivery (CISD).
- Order blocks formed after structure shifts can serve as refined entry points.
These allow flexibility without breaking the core logic of the model.

- The Twitter Model focuses on systematic liquidity raids paired with high-probability confirmations.
- Always anchor trades around previous day’s high/low for context.
- Entries should be filtered with time-based levels (midnight or daily open).
- SMT + MSS = confirmation
- The strategy is fractal, meaning you can trade any timeframe alignment depending on your trading style.

chunks.t:
A broadening formation occurs when price keeps expanding beyond a defined range without holding a breakout. Imagine price trapped inside a consolidation, only to constantly sweep one side, then the other. Over time, this creates a pattern of expansion both up and down, leading to a broader range than where it started.
Key features:
- Price takes out one side of a range, fails, and trades back inside
- The same process repeats, expanding both sides
- The result is a megaphone-style structure that highlights liquidity hunts

chunks.h: How to Spot and Draw Broadening Formations
chunks.t:
There are two common approaches:
- High-Low Method
- Identify a significant high and lowLook left to see which highs or lows were taken outConnect these points and extend them outward as the range expands
- Liquidity-Based MethodIdentify buy-side and sell-side liquidity sweepsEach time liquidity is taken, extend a line from that pointContinue this process as price expands, building out the broadening formation step by step
This approach keeps you focused on liquidity hunts rather than arbitrary points.

chunks.t:

- Targets: Use the edges of the broadening formation as liquidity targets

chunks.t:
On daily or higher charts, a broadening formation appears as an outside bar, where both the high and low of the previous day are taken. Extending these levels forward provides:
- Reversal zones
- Liquidity targets
- Context for intraday setups
Example: If the daily candle takes both the prior high and low, intraday traders can treat that bar as a higher-timeframe broadening formation.

chunks.h: Broadening Formations in the Seek & Destroy Daily Profile
chunks.t:
The ICT Seek & Destroy profile thrives on identifying false breakouts. Broadening formations naturally complement this idea.
- If London sweeps Asia’s high and low without displacing, expect New York to respect London’s range as a new broadening formation
- If multiple sessions fail to displace, the daily profile may remain choppy, and broadening formations help frame liquidity hunts throughout the day
These setups are especially effective during quieter news days or when the market is anticipating a major economic event. In those conditions, broadening formations often frame the back-and-forth liquidity hunts that define the day’s structure.

Broadening formations are more than just chart patterns. They provide a clear way to see how price sweeps liquidity, fails to break out, and shifts direction. When combined with ICT concepts such as SMT, Power of Three, session ranges, and higher timeframe outside bars, they become a reliable tool for anticipating price behavior. Instead of being caught off guard by choppy price action, you can recognize the natural rhythm of expansion and reversal within the market.

note: **SUMMARY:**  
The lesson explains what a broadening formation (megaphone pattern) is, how to identify and draw it using the High‑Low or Liquidity‑Based methods, and why it matters for spotting liquidity hunts, setting targets, and anticipating reversals. It shows how the pattern ties into ICT concepts such as the Power of Three, SMT divergence, session‑range boxes, and the Seek & Destroy daily profile, giving traders a framework to trade choppy, expanding markets on any timeframe.
**KEY RULES:**  
- A broadening formation occurs when price repeatedly takes out one side of a range, fails, and then trades back inside, expanding both higher highs and lower lows.  
- **High‑Low Method:** Identify a significant high and low, look left to see which prior highs/lows were taken out, connect those points and extend the lines outward as the range widens.  
- **Liquidity‑Based Method:** Identify each buy‑side or sell‑side liquidity sweep; each time liquidity is taken, extend a line from that point and continue the process as price expands.  
- Use the outer edges of the megaphone as **liquidity targets** for entries and exits.  
- If a breakout holds, the breakout side can become **support or resistance** (support/resistance flip).

note: - Look for **SMT divergence** at the edges of the formation to refine entry timing.  
- In a **range‑play**, expect price to move from one side of the megaphone to the other before a directional move.  
- Combine with ICT **Power of Three**: the formation often represents the Manipulation phase where both liquidity sides are swept.  
- Use **Discount/Premium** to mark equilibrium of the initial consolidation; price may revert to this level if higher‑timeframe order flow aligns.  
- Apply **Box Setup**: use Asia, London, New York session highs/lows as the initial box; the broadening formation builds around these session ranges.  
- On daily or higher charts, a broadening formation appears as an **outside bar** (both prior high and low taken); extend those levels forward for reversal zones and liquidity targets.  
- In the **Seek & Destroy daily profile**, if London sweeps Asia’s high/low without displacement, expect New York to respect London’s range as a new broadening formation; multiple session failures keep the profile choppy and highlight liquidity hunts.  
**DEFINITIONS:**  
- **Broadening Formation:** A megaphone‑shaped pattern where price makes higher highs and lower lows, expanding the range without a clean breakout.

note: - **High‑Low Method:** Spotting the formation by connecting the most extreme swing high and swing low and extending those trendlines outward.  
- **Liquidity‑Based Method:** Drawing the formation by extending lines from each point where buy‑side or sell‑side liquidity is taken.  
- **SMT Divergence:** Smart Money Technique divergence used at the edges of the formation to confirm entry signals.  
- **Power of Three:** ICT framework of Accumulation → Manipulation → Distribution; the broadening formation typically aligns with the Manipulation phase.  
- **Discount/Premium:** Equilibrium levels of the initial range; price may revert to these when higher‑timeframe order flow supports it.  
- **Box Setup (Session Ranges):** Using the high/low of Asia, London, and New York sessions as the initial consolidation box for the formation.  
- **Outside Bar (HTF):** A daily (or higher) candle that takes both the prior high and low, representing a higher‑timeframe broadening formation.  
- **Seek & Destroy Daily Profile:** ICT daily profile that highlights false breakouts; broadening formations help frame the liquidity hunts within this profile.  
**MISTAKES / INVALIDATION:**

note: - The formation is invalid if a breakout **holds** and the price does not return to the opposite side of the megaphone; the pattern then transitions to a new structure.  
- Do not rely on arbitrary points; use true liquidity sweeps or extreme swing points as the lesson stresses.  
- Ignoring the **session‑range box** or higher‑timeframe context can lead to misreading the pattern’s intent.

- *Diagram 2 (How to spot – High‑Low):* Candlestick chart with two horizontal lines at the extreme high and low of the initial consolidation box, illustrating the start of the expansion.  
- *Diagram 3 (Liquidity‑Based method):* Chart showing successive liquidity sweeps with lines extended from each sweep, building the broadening shape step‑by‑step.

Intermediate-term highs and lows are simply multiple short term highs and lows that create stronger pivot points:
- An intermediate-term low forms when a short-term low has another short-term low to its left and right.
- An intermediate-term high forms when a short-term high has another short-term high to its left and right.
There are two types:
- Basic intermediate-term structures (built off short-term swings).
- Rebalanced intermediate-term structures (formed when price rebalances a fair value gap and trades away).

chunks.t:
Long-term structures are anchored on higher time frame reactions.
- A long-term low is confirmed when price reacts from a higher timeframe level, then forms a short-term low on each side.
- A long-term high follows the same logic but off a higher timeframe level.
Once long-term highs or lows are set, traders anticipate intermediate-term and short-term structure shifts around them.

Market structure shifts (MSS) and breaks of structure (BOS) are clearer once you know the hierarchy:
- Short-term highs/lows show local price reactions.
- Intermediate-term highs/lows confirm stronger pivots and sweeps (protected swings).
- Long-term highs/lows set the broader framework for where price is likely heading.

When the market is clean, fair value gaps and order blocks can provide clear trade setups. But when price is choppy, advanced market structure helps filter entries:
- Look for short-term highs/lows to confirm shifts.
- Use intermediate-term sweeps as confirmation of continuation or reversal.
- Anchor expectations around long-term levels drawn from higher timeframes.
This layered approach prevents premature entries and helps align trades with broader price delivery.

- Short-term highs/lows are the foundation.
- Intermediate-term structures confirm strength and sweeps.
- Long-term highs/lows are tied to higher timeframe reactions.
- Advanced market structure helps navigate messy price action when clean imbalances are absent.

SUMMARY: This lesson explains how to identify and use short‑term, intermediate‑term, and long‑term market structure pivots in price action trading. It teaches that short‑term highs and lows are the building blocks, intermediate‑term pivots are formed by clustering multiple short‑term pivots, and long‑term pivots are anchored to higher‑time‑frame reactions. Understanding this hierarchy allows traders to filter entries, confirm sweeps, and align trades with the broader market direction.

KEY RULES: - A short‑term low (STL) forms when a swing low has a higher low on each side.  
- A short‑term high (STH) forms when a swing high has a lower high on each side.  
- An intermediate‑term low forms when a short‑term low has another short‑term low to its left and right.  
- An intermediate‑term high forms when a short‑term high has another short‑term high to its left and right.  
- Intermediate‑term structures can be basic (built off short‑term swings) or rebalanced (formed when price rebalances a fair value gap and trades away).  
- A long‑term low is confirmed when price reacts from a higher‑time‑frame level, then forms a short‑term low on each side.  
- A long‑term high follows the same logic but off a higher‑time‑frame level.  
- Market structure shifts (MSS) and breaks of structure (BOS) are clearer once the hierarchy is known.  
- When the market is clean, fair value gaps and order blocks provide clear trade setups; when price is choppy, use advanced market structure to filter entries.  
- Look for short‑term highs/lows to confirm shifts, use intermediate‑term sweeps as confirmation of continuation or reversal, and anchor expectations around long‑term levels drawn from higher timeframes.

DEFINITIONS: - **Short‑term high (STH)** – a swing high with lower highs on both sides (3‑ or 5‑candle formation where the center has the highest high).  
- **Short‑term low (STL)** – a swing low with higher lows on both sides (3‑ or 5‑candle formation where the center has the lowest low).  
- **Intermediate‑term high (ITH)** – a high formed when a short‑term high has another short‑term high to its left and right.  
- **Intermediate‑term low (ITL)** – a low formed when a short‑term low has another short‑term low to its left and right.  
- **Long‑term high (LTH)** – a high confirmed when price reacts from a higher‑time‑frame level and then forms a short‑term high on each side.  
- **Long‑term low (LTL)** – a low confirmed when price reacts from a higher‑time‑frame level and then forms a short‑term low on each side.  
- **Market structure shift (MSS)** – a change in the direction of market structure.  
- **Break of structure (BOS)** – a price move that invalidates the previous structure level.  
- **Fair value gap** – an imbalance in price that can be used to identify potential order block levels.  
- **Order block** – a cluster of orders that can act as support or resistance.  
- **Sweep (protected swing)** – a strong move that confirms the strength of an intermediate‑term pivot.

If you’ve been studying smart money concepts, you’ve probably heard of order blocks. Order blocks are key price areas where institutions accumulate positions before a move. But there’s a more refined concept built off order blocks called the propulsion block, which can give you even sharper trade entries and insights.
In this guide, we’ll quickly review order blocks, then dive deep into propulsion blocks with clear explanations and examples.

An order block is essentially the footprint of institutional activity.
- Bearish order block: A series of up-close candles into an important level, followed by displacement lower and a close below the candle(s).
- Bullish order block: A series of down-close candles into an important level, followed by displacement higher and a close above the candle(s).
When price returns to these areas, traders expect it to react and move away, since they represent institutional buying or selling zones.

A propulsion block is an order block that forms directly off another order block.
Here’s the sequence:
1. Price forms a valid order block (bullish or bearish).
2. Price retraces into that order block.
3. A new opposite candle (down-close for bullish or up-close for bearish) forms inside the order block.
4. Displacement occurs, confirming a propulsion block.
Key things to note about propulsion blocks:
- The opening price of the propulsion block is highly sensitive.
- Price should not close beyond the mean threshold of the block.
- They often act as refined levels, offering precision entries.

chunks.h: Practical Guidelines for Using Propulsion Blocks
chunks.t:
- Always confirm displacement before labeling a propulsion block.
- Use the opening price as the primary entry reference.
- Respect the mean threshold—if price closes beyond it, the block loses validity.
- Combine with liquidity concepts (highs/lows sweeps, fair value gaps) for stronger confluence.

Propulsion blocks are simply an advanced evolution of order blocks, allowing traders to refine entries and understand institutional footprints more clearly. By focusing on sensitivity at the opening price and guarding against mean threshold violations, traders can use propulsion blocks as reliable continuation or reversal levels.
